propositions.text: Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX is a Haitian citizen appealing the RPD's October 30, 2018 decision rejecting his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX is a citizen of Haiti. He appeals the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rendered on October 30, 2018, rejecting his claim filed pursuant to sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the Act).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant is a Haitian citizen appealing the RPD's October 30, 2018 decision rejecting his refugee claim.

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant not credible due to important omissions and contradictions in his evidence.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the appellant was not credible as to the basis of his claim, due to important omissions and contradictions in the appellant's evidence.

propositions.text: The appellant contests the RPD's credibility conclusions and argues the RPD erred in analyzing his prospective fear.
propositions.quote: The appellant contests the RPD's credibility conclusions and submits that the RPD erred in the analysis of his prospective fear.

propositions.text: The appellant asks the RAD to grant the appeal or return the file to the RPD for a new examination.
propositions.quote: They ask the Refugee Appeals Division (RAD) to grant the appeal or to return the file to the RPD for a new examination.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the appellant not credible; the appellant contests this and asks the RAD to grant the appeal or remit the case.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges a 2001 attack by criminal 'XXXX' from 'XXXX XXXX' and his escape to his uncle's house.
propositions.quote: In his Basis of Claim form the appellant alleges that on XXXX XXXX, 2001, criminal "XXXX" from the XXXX XXXX came to his house in order to kill him. He was able to escape to his uncle's house, where he XXXX XXXX because of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: The appellant stayed with his uncle's friend until leaving the country by boat to the 'XXXX' in 2001.
propositions.quote: His uncle took care of him and took him to XXXX XXXX where he stayed with his uncle's friend until XXXX XXXX, 2001, when he left the country by boat to go to the XXXX.

propositions.text: The appellant arrived in the US in 2001 and claimed political asylum, which was rejected for insufficient details.
propositions.quote: The appellant arrived in the United States on XXXX XXXX, 2001, where he made a claim for political asylum. His claim was rejected because the claimant had not provided enough details.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges a 2001 attack, escape, stay with relatives, and a rejected US asylum claim for lack of details.

propositions.text: In 2008, the appellant married and had three children; his wife's sponsorship application was denied.
propositions.quote: In 2008, the appellant got married and had three children. His wife sponsored him but the application was denied.

propositions.text: The appellant arrived in Canada in 2017 and claimed asylum the same year.
propositions.quote: He arrived in Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2017, and claimed asylum on XXXX XXXX, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant married in 2008, was denied sponsorship, arrived in Canada in 2017, and claimed asylum.

propositions.text: On hearing day, the appellant amended his BOC to add OPL membership from 2000 to 2001.
propositions.quote: On the day of the hearing, the appellant amended his BOC to add that he had been an active member of the OPL from XXXX 2000 to XXXX 2001.

propositions.text: During 2000 elections, Lavalas militias opposed results favoring OPL, leading to appellant's alleged persecution.
propositions.quote: During the November 2000 elections, the militias of the Lavalas party took the streets to oppose the elections results favoring OPL. Following that, the appellant underwent what has been summarized above.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant amended his claim to add OPL membership and described election-related persecution in 2000.

propositions.text: The court shares some RPD concerns about appellant's credibility and finds no established prospective risk based on political activities.
propositions.quote: Based on my independent analysis of all the evidence on the file, including the recording of the hearing, I share some of the RPD's concerns with respect to the appellant's credibility and find that the appellant has not established a prospective risk in Haiti based on his political activities.

paragraphs.summary: The court shares some RPD credibility concerns and finds no established prospective risk from appellant's political activities.

propositions.text: The appeal is rejected.
propositions.quote: The appeal is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the appeal.

propositions.text: The RAD independently assesses all evidence and correctness is the applicable standard of review here.
propositions.quote: The RAD is required to independently assess all the evidence and determine whether the RPD was correct in relation to each alleged error of law, fact or mixed fact and law. In exceptional situations, where the RAD finds that the RPD had a meaningful advantage, it will defer to its findings and reasons will be provided in that situation.1 In this case, the applicable standard of review is that of correctness.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD independently assesses evidence and applies the correctness standard of review in this case.

propositions.text: Claimant's sworn evidence is presumed truthful unless valid reasons to doubt exist.
propositions.quote: Generally, a claimant's evidence given under oath is presumed to be truthful, unless there are valid reasons to doubt it.

propositions.text: There are sufficient problems with appellant's evidence to seriously doubt credibility of essential claim elements.
propositions.quote: In this case, there are sufficient problems with the appellant's evidence to cast a serious doubt as to the credibility of certain essential elements of his claim, as explained below.

paragraphs.summary: The court states sworn evidence is presumed truthful but finds serious credibility doubts in appellant's essential claim elements.

propositions.text: Appellant's failure to mention OPL membership in original BOC is problematic and explanation is unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I find it problematic that the appellant failed to mention in his original BOC that he was a member of the OPL from XXXX 2000 to XXXX 2001, in light of the fact that this is the central element of his asylum claim and the reason why XXXX XXXX XXXX allegedly attacked him.

propositions.text: Appellant's claim of inadequate counsel advice lacks weight without following IRB procedure.
propositions.quote: I do not find the appellant's explanation for the late amendment, namely that he had been inadequately advised by his counsel, reasonable. Allegations against a counsel can be given no weight unless the appellant follows the procedure established by the IRB to this effect.

propositions.text: The RPD found appellant's amendment about OPL membership inconsistent with asylum form indicating only 'protester' status.
propositions.quote: I also agree with the RPD that his amendment to the effect that he was a member of the OPL is inconsistent with his asylum form IMM-5669 where the appellant only indicated that his political implication was as a "protester" against the Lavalas.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's omission of OPL membership problematic, rejects counsel excuse, and agrees with RPD on inconsistency with asylum form.

propositions.text: Appellant's testimony that OPL was eliminated in first election tour contradicts his BOC amendment about Lavalas militia protests.
propositions.quote: The appellant testified that OPL was eliminated in the first tour of the elections. This is, however, contradictory to his BOC amendment, where he says that Lavalas militia took the streets to protest the 2000 election results that were in favour of the OPL.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's testimony about OPL elimination contradicts his BOC amendment about Lavalas militia protests.

propositions.text: Appellant's testimony about Independent Party membership and activities is absent from BOC and amendment, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The appellant further indicated in his testimony that during the second tour of the 2000 elections, he became a member of the Independent Party and that he worked on immobilizing the population to vote against Lavalas. He was supporting the Independent Party's candidate, M. Arnold Dumas. None of this information appears in his original BOC, nor in his amendment. As such, I do not believe the appellant that he was indeed a member of the OPL, nor a member of the Independent Party.

paragraphs.summary: The court disbelieves appellant's claimed Independent Party membership and activities due to absence in BOC and amendment.

propositions.text: Appellant's testimony about fearing current 'XXXX XXXX' and recognition is omitted from written narrative, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the appellant indicated in his testimony that he fears the current XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and who would recognize him because they XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and he had XXXX XXXX XXXX of the appellant's sister. However, no mention is made of this in the appellant's written narrative.

propositions.text: The RPD found omission of risk-related information unreasonable, especially given prior US asylum rejection for lack of details.
propositions.quote: I agree with this RPD that it is not reasonable for the appellant to have omitted this information which relates directly to the risk he would face if he returned to Haiti, especially in light of the fact that his asylum claim in the United States had been rejected for lack of sufficient details.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows 'XXXX XXXX XXXX' is not current 'XXXX XXXX' but another entity.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, according to the documentary evidence, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is not the current XXXX XXXX, but rather the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: The appellant adjusted testimony to amplify risk; court disbelieves close relationship with 'XXXX XXXX XXXX' and risk posed.
propositions.quote: Based on the foregoing, I am of the view that the appellant adjusted his testimony in order to amplify the risk faced. I therefore do not believe that the appellant had a close relationship with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and that the latter poses a risk to the appellant if he returned to Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant omitted risk details, adjusted testimony to amplify risk, and disbelieves claimed close relationship posing risk.

propositions.text: Even if allegations are true, appellant has not established a prospective risk if returned to Haiti.
propositions.quote: However, even if I were to accept these allegations as being true, I am of the view that the appellant has not established a prospective risk, if he returned to Haiti, as explained below.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant has not established prospective risk even if allegations are true.

propositions.text: Risk analysis is prospective, assessing serious possibility of persecution or risks under section 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: It is worth mentioning that the analysis of the risk that a claimant faces in their country of origin is prospective in nature. That means that the tribunal must evaluate if, on the basis of the events lived by the appellant, his personal profile and the objective country documentation, the tribunal arrives at the conclusion that the appellant has established that he will be exposed to a serious possibility of persecution or, on a balance of probabilities, to any of the risks enumerated in section 97 of the Act, namely a risk to his life, torture or cruel and inhumane treatments or punishments, should he return to his country.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains risk analysis is prospective, assessing serious possibility of persecution or risks under section 97 of the Act.

propositions.text: Whether appellant faces a prospective risk in Haiti due to his profile and political activities.
propositions.quote: A significant issue is this case is the degree to which the appellant faces a prospective risk in Haiti. The documentary evidence does not establish that the appellant's profile, his past or future political work with the OPL would put him at risk as defined in sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the issue of whether appellant faces prospective risk in Haiti from his profile and political activities.

propositions.text: Events occurred almost 20 years ago; no evidence appellant is still sought by 'XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX'.
propositions.quote: Firstly, the events as related by the appellant took place almost 20 years ago. The appellant has not established that he is still being actively sought by the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Even if appellant was OPL or Independent Party member, no evidence he continued political involvement or intends to return to politics.
propositions.quote: Even if I accept that he was a member of the OPL from XXXX 2000 to XXXX 2001, or of the Independent Party, the appellant has not established that he has continued to be implicated in Haitian politics, nor has he expressed a desire to do so if he was to return to Haiti.

propositions.text: Appellant testified OPL no longer exists, contrary to documentary evidence.
propositions.quote: In fact, the appellant testified that he believed that OPL doe not exist anymore, which is contrary to the documentary evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds events are 20 years old, no evidence of ongoing political involvement or risk, and appellant's belief OPL no longer exists is incorrect.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence does not support risk from political activity with OPL or Independent Party.
propositions.quote: Although election violence and instances of intimidation occur, the documentary evidence does not support the conclusion that political activity with the OPL would put him at risk of persecution or other serious mistreatment.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows armed gangs called 'XXXX' supported Aristide's return in 2000 and committed acts of terror.
propositions.quote: The documentary evidence does indicate that armed gangs called "XXXX" who supported Aristide's return to power in early 2000 were responsible for "acts of terror".

propositions.text: No serious possibility that past violence will recur due to appellant's past political activities.
propositions.quote: However, the documentary evidence does not establish a serious possibility that the violence lived by the appellant then is likely to occur again because of his past activities with the OPL or with the Independent Party.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds documentary evidence shows past violence but no serious possibility it will recur due to appellant's past political activities.

propositions.text: 2017 report shows political violence in Haiti has diminished substantially; no systemic oppression of opposition.
propositions.quote: According to a report by the Office Français de protection des réfugiés et apatrides, dated 2017, the tendency towards political violence has diminished substantially in recent years. There is currently no systemic oppression of political opposition in Haiti, who are able to enjoy their civil and political rights freely.

propositions.text: NGO monitoring human rights violations is unaware of current persecution against OPL members.
propositions.quote: The National Human Rights Defense Network, an NGO that monitors human rights violations committed by the state in Haiti, is not aware of current persecution against OPL members in Haiti.

propositions.text: Representative of Haitian Human Rights Organizations states no more problems for OPL than other parties; no files on OPL members.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, as per a representative of the Platform of Haitian Human Rights Organizations "there are a number of general protection problems in Haiti, but there are no more problems for this party [OPL] than for others". The same source stated that the POHDH has no files concerning OPL members, but "[that] some OPL members have been victims of generalized violence".

paragraphs.summary: The court finds reports show diminished political violence, no systemic oppression, and no current persecution of OPL members.

propositions.text: Appellant has not established a political profile exposing him to risk beyond generalized violence experienced by all Haitians.
propositions.quote: I am of the view that the appellant has not established that he has a political profile such that he would risk being a victim of political violence, other than the generalized evidence experienced by all Haitians.

propositions.text: Even if recognized by 'XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX', no evidence he would be harmed for past political involvement two decades ago.
propositions.quote: Even if I were to accept that he will be recognized by XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX if he returns to Haiti, there is no evidence that the latter would harm the appellant for his alleged implication with the OPL or the Independent Party two decades ago.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant has not shown a political profile risking targeted violence beyond generalized violence, nor evidence of harm if recognized.

propositions.text: The RPD concluded the appellant does not have a well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: The RPD was correct in concluding that the appellant does not have a well-founded fear or persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD correctly found the appellant lacks a well-founded fear of persecution, as stated by the earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD decision that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection under sections 96 and 97 of the Act.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to subsection 111 (1) (a) of the Act, the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD pursuant to which the appellant is neither a Convention refugee, nor a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97 of the Act.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's decision that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection, per the court.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
